problems.title: Change logarithm bases before simplifying
problems.question: Evaluate (log₂49)/(log₁₈7)−4log₂1.5.
problems.idea: Use the change-of-base rule.
steps: The quotient is 2log₂18.
Since 18=2·3² and 1.5=3/2, the expression is 2(1+2log₂3)−4(log₂3−1)=6.

problems.title: A right triangle inscribed in a sphere
problems.question: A sphere of radius 17 contains a right triangle with legs 10 and 24 on its surface. Find the centre’s distance from the triangle plane.
problems.idea: The plane-section circle is the triangle’s circumcircle.
steps: The distance is √120=2√30.

problems.title: Range of an exponential with a bounded exponent
problems.question: Find the range of y=4^{x/(x²+1)}.
problems.idea: Use squares to bound the exponent.
steps: The endpoints occur at x=−1 and x=1. The exponent is continuous and attains all intermediate values.
Since base 4 is increasing, the output range is [4^(−1/2),4^(1/2)].

problems.title: Maximize the argument of an increasing logarithm
problems.question: Find the maximum of log₄(8−|3|x|−8|) on [1/3,4].
problems.idea: The absolute value is minimized at zero.
steps: x=8/3 belongs to the interval and makes the absolute value zero.
The maximum is log₄8=3/2.

problems.title: Count odd exponential functions
problems.question: Among the six printed exponential functions, how many are odd?
problems.idea: An odd function has f(−x)=−f(x), in particular f(0)=0.
steps: This difference changes sign under x→−x, so it is odd.
The other five functions are positive at x=0, so none can be odd.

problems.title: A logarithm with base below one
problems.question: Find the maximum of log₀.₂(4x²+4x+6).
problems.idea: A logarithm with base between 0 and 1 decreases as its argument increases.
steps: The maximum occurs at the smallest argument, 5.
log₀.₂5=−1 because (1/5)^(−1)=5.

problems.title: An exponential equation with two roots
problems.question: Find the least integer greater than the solution(s) of 2^{x²−x−6}=3^{x−3}.
problems.idea: Take natural logarithms and factor x−3.
steps: The equation is (x−3)[(x+2)ln2−ln3]=0.
The two roots are x=3 and x=log₂3−2≈−0.415.
The least integer greater than both roots is 4. For the smaller root alone it would be 0.
problems.answer: 4 if an integer above every solution is intended.
problems.note: The equation has two roots. The singular wording “the solution” is incomplete; 4 is the listed answer above both.

problems.title: A projection onto a sphere’s tangent plane
problems.question: A lies on a sphere of radius 13. AB is perpendicular to a tangent plane, B lies on it, and AB=1. Find OB, where O is the sphere centre.
problems.idea: Use the radius perpendicular to the tangent plane.
formulas: Let T be the contact point. OT=13, and A is at normal distance 12 from the centre toward the plane.
steps: The in-plane offset TB has square 13²−12²=25.
Triangle OTB is right, so OB²=13²+25=194.

problems.title: A logarithmic equation becomes linear in ln x
problems.question: Solve log₂x+log₃x=2log₂6.
problems.idea: Convert every logarithm to natural logarithms.
steps: Because ln6=ln2+ln3, cancellation gives ln x=2ln3.
Thus x=9, which is positive.

problems.title: An exponential inequality for every real input
problems.question: Find a such that a·3ˣ+a>1 for every real x.
problems.idea: 3ˣ ranges over all positive numbers and approaches zero.
steps: If a≥1 it is strictly greater than 1 for every t>0, including when a=1.
If a<1, a sufficiently small positive t makes the inequality fail; nonpositive a fails immediately.

problems.title: Two types of lateral face in a square-base pyramid
problems.question: A pyramid has square base and one lateral edge perpendicular to the base. A larger lateral-face area is twice a smaller one and equals 6√3. Find the base area.
problems.idea: There are two congruent faces of each of two types.
formulas: For base edge a and vertical edge h, small face=ah/2; large face=a√(a²+h²)/2.
steps: The area ratio 2 gives √(a²+h²)=2h, so a²=3h².
The large area is a·(2a/√3)/2=a²/√3=6√3.
Therefore a²=18.

problems.title: Integers in a logarithmic range
problems.question: How many integers lie in the range of log₂[(sin x+cos x+3√2)/√2]?
problems.idea: Bound sin x+cos x between −√2 and √2.
steps: An increasing base-2 logarithm maps this to [1,2].
The integers in the interval are 1 and 2.

problems.title: An exponential-log system with symmetric roots
problems.question: Find x+y if x^{lg y}=2 and xy=20.
problems.idea: Take base-10 logarithms and set u=lg x,v=lg y.
steps: Thus u,v are roots of t²−(1+lg2)t+lg2=(t−1)(t−lg2).

problems.title: Intersecting diagonals of adjacent prism faces
problems.question: All edges of a regular hexagonal prism are equal. Find the cosine of the angle between intersecting diagonals of adjacent lateral faces.
problems.idea: Use the two diagonals through their shared upper vertex.
formulas: Their horizontal components are adjacent hexagon sides with angle 120°; their vertical components both have length a.
steps: The dot product is a²cos120°+a²=a²/2.
Each diagonal has length a√2.
Divide by 2a².

problems.title: A logarithm of a bounded cosine
problems.question: Find the range of y=log₂(5+3cos x).
problems.idea: First bound the positive argument.
steps: Apply the increasing logarithm: log₂2≤y≤log₂8.

problems.title: Lateral area of a regular triangular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base edge twice its apothem. Its base area is 2 cm². Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Compare both areas as multiples of a².
formulas: Apothem l=a/2; base area=√3a²/4; lateral area=3al/2=3a²/4.
steps: The ratio lateral/base is √3.
Multiply the base area 2 by √3.

problems.title: Count roots using a strictly convex function
problems.question: How many real roots satisfy x²−2x−log₂|1−x|=3?
problems.idea: Set t=|x−1|>0, then count the positive t-roots.
steps: F is strictly convex, tends to +∞ as t→0+ and as t→∞, and F(1)=1<4.
Hence the horizontal line y=4 meets it exactly twice.
Each positive t gives the two distinct values x=1±t. Different t values give different x.

problems.title: A cone from a centre-to-generator distance
problems.question: A cone has base radius 15 cm. The distance from the base centre to a generator is 12 cm. Find the height.
problems.idea: Use the right triangle in an axial section.
steps: 12=15h/√(225+h²). Squaring gives 144(225+h²)=225h².
Thus 81h²=32400, so h=20.

problems.title: Reflect a graph across a horizontal line
problems.question: Reflect y=1−log₂(2x+3) across y=4. Find the new equation.
problems.idea: A reflection across y=c maps y to 2c−y.
steps: Simplify the expression, retaining the original domain x>−3/2.

problems.title: Volume from two base diagonals
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base diagonals 6 and 8 with angle 30°. Its shorter space diagonal makes 45° with the base. Find the volume.
problems.idea: The short space diagonal projects to the shorter base diagonal.
steps: Base area=6·8·(1/2)/2=12. Height=6.
Volume=12·6.

problems.title: A product of two logarithms factors
problems.question: Which interval contains the root of lg(x−10)lg(x+10)=lg(x²−100)−1?
problems.idea: Use the domain x>10 and combine the log of the product.
steps: This gives (u−1)(v−1)=0.
u=1 gives x=20. v=1 gives x=0, outside the domain.
Therefore the root lies in (18,21).

problems.title: A decreasing logarithm reverses a range
problems.question: Find the range of log₀.₁[300/(1+lg(100+x²))].
problems.idea: Bound the inner denominator and keep the sign of the log base in mind.
formulas: lg(100+x²)≥2; the full argument ranges over (0,100].
steps: At x=0 the argument is 100, giving log₀.₁100=−2.
As |x| grows, the argument tends to 0 and the logarithm tends to +∞.
All intermediate outputs occur continuously.
problems.note: The printed interval [2,+∞) has the wrong sign at its lower endpoint; the correct lower endpoint is −2.

problems.title: A sphere inscribed in a right triangular prism
problems.question: A right triangular prism has base hypotenuse 7 and an inscribed sphere of radius 1 touching every face. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: The prism height is the sphere diameter and the base inradius is 1.
formulas: h=2; for a right triangle r=(a+b−c)/2.
steps: a+b=7+2=9, so the base perimeter is 16.
Lateral area=perimeter×height=16·2.

problems.title: Possible angles between three skew directions
problems.question: Angles between a,b and b,c are 10° and 70°. Which listed value can be the angle between a,c?
problems.idea: The possible smaller direction angles range from the difference to the sum.
steps: Thus 60°≤θ≤80°. Of the listed values only 65° is in that interval.
Translations can make the lines skew without changing their directions.

problems.title: A cone whose net is a semicircle
problems.question: The cone’s lateral net is a semicircle of diameter 6. Find its height.
problems.idea: The net radius is the slant height; its arc is the base circumference.
